items.title: Post-Quantum Questions to Ask Your Vendors
items.desc: CISA, the Australian Signals Directorate’s Australian Cyber Security Centre (ASD’s ACSC) and the National Security Agency (NSA) released joint guidance and an accompanying quick-reference list to help organizations assess vendor readiness for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). As quantum computing advances, widely used public-key cryptography will become vulnerable to compromise from cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). To protect their systems and data, organizations must plan for and transition to PQC—which includes algorithms capable of withstanding both classical computing and quantum-enabled threats—before CRQCs become available. Many organizations rely on third-party vendors for managed services, cloud capabilities, and other cryptography-dependent products and services. Cryptography is also embedded in systems and devices that are difficult to update, tied to long asset lifecycles, and require vendor support or replacement—such as industrial control systems and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Reliance on vendors means that effective PQC transition depends on vendor readiness, and early, structured engagement with these vendors is critical to planning efforts. Organizations can use the vendor-neutral questions outlined in this guidance to determine whether a vendor understands quantum-related risks, maintains transparency over its cryptographic implementations, and supports a secure, cost-effective and timely transition to PQC. Visit CISA’s PQC Initiative page for additional resources.

items.desc: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2024-27834 Apple Multiple Products Improper Authentication Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.desc: La Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés s’est réunie le jeudi 22 octobre 2026 à 9 h 30 avec l’ordre du jour suivant :

items.title: Journée RGPD à Poitiers : cybersécurité, IA et conformité au cœur des enjeux de protection des données
items.desc: La CNIL organise une nouvelle Journée RGPD à Poitiers le 1er décembre 2026. Cet évènement sera l’occasion d’échanger avec les acteurs du territoire sur les actualités en matière de protection des données personnelles et les enjeux concrets auxquels sont confrontés les professionnels.

items.title: Revoir le webinaire - Nouveau régime de la prospection téléphonique : comment et quand recueillir le consentement de la personne concernée ?
items.desc: La CNIL vous propose de décrypter un sujet ou une actualité en lien avec la protection des données à travers une série de webinaires. Retrouvez ce nouvel épisode consacré à la prospection téléphonique.

items.title: Multiples vulnérabilités dans Roundcube Webmail (19 octobre 2026)
items.desc: De multiples vulnérabilités ont été découvertes dans Roundcube Webmail. Certaines d'entre elles permettent à un attaquant de provoquer une exécution de code arbitraire à distance, une falsification de requêtes côté serveur (SSRF) et une injection de code indirecte à distance (XSS).

items.title: De la protection des données à la création de valeur en finance : des autorités européennes publient une étude et des bonnes pratiques
items.desc: La CNIL, l’ICO et la CNPD publient leur étude conjointe « De la protection des données à la création de valeur en finance : évaluation des données, comptabilité, fusions-acquisitions et gouvernance », rassemblant analyses et bonnes pratiques à destination des entreprises et des acteurs financiers.

items.title: Reconstitution d’adresses électroniques professionnelles : dans quel cadre est-ce autorisé ?
items.desc: La reconstitution d’adresses électroniques professionnelles à partir de données accessibles en ligne est utilisée pour contacter des interlocuteurs, notamment dans le cadre de la prospection. Elle est encadrée par le RGPD et ne peut reposer sur l’intérêt légitime que si certaines conditions sont remplies.
